newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firmer on debt prepayment.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firmer on debt prepayment.

text.p: The Mexican peso gathered strength from early trade to stand firmer at mid-morning on Tuesday after news of sovereign debt prepayment and strong industrial activity data encouraged dealers to sell dollars, traders said.
"The debt prepayment announcement is making a big impact, and dealers began to sell long dollar positions, as they were too expensive to hold on to," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were 0.5 and 0.4 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9425/7.9450 and 7.9390/7.9420 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed 1.2 centavos firmer at 7.9360/7.9390 per dollar.
Mexico's Finance Ministry announced debt refinancing, including a decision to prepay $6 billion in floating-rate bank notes and the issue of $1 billion in five-year floating-rate bonds.

The Ministry had earlier announced industrial activity in April rose by 15 percent compared to the same month last year. Financial firms previously surveyed by Reuters MEX22 had expected an increase of 7.92 percent.
"The market has been somewhat volatile in response to the (U.S.) long bond, but now I see dollars in the market," another trader said.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were meanwhile off 8/32 to yield 6.71 percent. ((--Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9555))
